conceptual assets.information: The software-visible clock-frequency word is held in the first system-information entry, which software and system integration depend on when reading the configured clock frequency. It is initialized from CLOCK_FREQUENCY and can be replaced by a bus write.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The word is directly mutable by bus_req_i.data on the clocked write at line 95, so an unauthorized write can corrupt the system information returned to software; the value is returned through bus_rsp_o.data at line 168.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker able to issue an unchecked write with bus_req_i.stb, bus_req_i.rw and the selected address can replace the clock-frequency word and cause software to receive incorrect system information.

considered, not kept.concept: Static hardware capability and build configuration descriptors
considered, not kept.reason: The descriptors at lines 102-150 are derived only from build-time generics and constants, so no run-time element can modify them; the RTL also shows no confidentiality or availability requirement for them.

bus_req_i.stb, bus_req_i.rw and bus_req_i.addr only select, write and time accesses at lines 94 and 161-162, so the access-command and held-address rules do not treat them as information pieces of their own.
buf_ack only re-times the request strobe at line 160 and drives the response acknowledge at line 169, so it is a bus-handshake copy rather than an independent asset.
buf_adr only copies the request address for selecting the returned system-information word at lines 162 and 168, so it is a held address used while the access is served.
clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset the internal registers at lines 89-97 and 154-164, and the clock/reset rule excludes them as conceptual assets.
